transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What has brought you in to see me today?

Um… I guess I’ve been a little stressed at work. I drive for transportation, and there’s been some stuff with dispatch and compliance that’s been hard to ignore.

Like, I know there’s normal oversight and everything, and I’m not trying to sound difficult, but it feels like they’re tracking my route changes through the computer system. And sometimes there are little comments on the radio that seem… pointed, I guess. Certain drivers seem like they’re reporting on me too. I just wanted to talk to someone about it and make sure I’m handling it the right way.

When you think about dispatch tracking your route changes and other drivers reporting on you, do you feel completely certain this is really happening, or do you see it as more of a worry that might be mistaken?

I mean… I don’t want to say “completely certain” in a way that sounds unreasonable. I understand there’s normal oversight with dispatch and compliance.

But it doesn’t feel like just a worry, if I’m being honest. The route changes show up in the computer system, and then the comments on the radio line up with things I’ve done. And certain drivers… it really seems like they’re reporting on me. I can tell, even if people say it’s just part of the job.
Have any supervisors or coworkers ever directly told you that they are tracking you or reporting on you, or is this something you’ve concluded from how things seem to line up?

No, not directly like that. Nobody’s pulled me aside and said, “We’re tracking you,” or anything.

It’s more… what I’ve concluded from how it lines up. Like dispatch and compliance can see the route changes in the system, I know that’s normal, but then the radio comments will be right after something happens, and certain drivers seem to know things or act like they’re reporting back. I realize that might sound like I’m reading into it, but it’s hard for me not to notice.
Aside from the situation with dispatch and the other drivers, do you find yourself worrying a lot about many different things in your life, to the point that it feels hard to control the worrying?

I don’t think so… not in a general way. I mean, I worry about normal things, like anyone does, bills or being on time, that kind of thing. But I wouldn’t say I’m worrying about everything all the time or that I can’t control it.

It’s more this work situation that’s been hard to let go of. I hope that makes sense.
When you step back from the situation and really think it through, do you feel it is actually possible that you might be misinterpreting what’s happening with dispatch and the other drivers?

I guess… yes, it’s possible. I don’t want to seem like I’m refusing to consider that.

But when I’m actually there, it doesn’t feel like I’m just making it up. The route changes are in the system, and then those little comments come over the radio, and certain drivers act like they know or like they’re reporting back. So I can say maybe I’m misinterpreting some of it, but it still really feels like something is going on.
Have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people around you didn’t seem to hear, when there wasn’t a clear source for them?

Um… no, I don’t think so. Not like a voice talking to me when nobody’s there or anything.

Sometimes with the radio or background noise I might think I heard something and then it’s nothing, but I think that happens to people, right? I haven’t had anything where I’m sure I’m hearing sounds other people can’t hear.
Has this sense that dispatch and other drivers are tracking or reporting on you led to any concrete problems at work, like write-ups, conflicts, or trouble doing your job?

A little, yeah… I mean, I’m still doing my job, I don’t want to make it sound like I’m falling apart or anything.

But I have gotten behind on route reports, and sometimes the instructions I give or follow get… kind of confusing, I guess. Drivers have complained a few times that things weren’t clear. It’s embarrassing to say that.

And at home, my husband’s been picking up more than usual—meals, phone calls, just basic planning—because I’m not really keeping up with it the way I normally would. Is that the kind of thing you mean?

When people you trust, like your husband or close friends, hear your concerns about dispatch and the other drivers, do you still feel sure that your explanation is right, or do their reactions ever seriously make you doubt that this is really happening?

I mean… I try to listen to my husband. He’s not dismissive, exactly, and I know he cares about me, so when he says it sounds like normal oversight or that maybe I’m reading too much into it, I do stop and think, “Okay, maybe.”

But honestly, it doesn’t make the feeling go away. I’m here because it still feels like dispatch and compliance are tracking my route changes through the computer system, and then there are these little comments on the radio that line up too closely. And certain drivers… it just seems like they’re reporting on me somehow.

I know that probably sounds like I’m not taking feedback well. I don’t want to be difficult. Their reactions make me question myself a little, but I still feel like my explanation is probably right.
Over the past month, has this situation at work been making you feel stressed or on edge almost every day, even when you’re not actually at work?

I’m not sure I’d say almost every day… I mean, maybe I don’t track it that closely.

It does follow me home sometimes, like I’ll still be thinking about it or feeling tense, but I try to tell myself not to make too big a deal out of it. I don’t want to sound dramatic. Maybe it’s more than I’d like, but I don’t know if I can say it’s every day.
Because of your sense that dispatch and the other drivers are tracking or reporting on you, have you actually avoided going in to work or called out when you otherwise wouldn’t have?

I haven’t really called out because of it, no… I mean, I’ve still been going in. I don’t want to be someone who just stops showing up.

It’s more that when I’m there, I’m not keeping up like I should. I’ve gotten behind on route reports, and I guess my instructions have been confusing enough that some drivers complained. And then at home my husband’s had to pick up meals and phone calls and planning stuff because I’m kind of not managing it the way I normally do.

So… not avoiding work exactly. More like I’m still going, but I’m not functioning as well. Is that what you’re asking?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a persistent, circumscribed belief that dispatch and certain drivers are tracking and reporting on her in a targeted way. This belief is based on subjective interpretations (timing of radio comments, others' behavior) without direct confirmation, is held with strong conviction, and persists despite reassurance from her husband and lack of objective evidence. It is not a culturally sanctioned belief, is not better explained by generalized anxiety or a primary mood disorder, and is associated with functional decline at work and at home. The content is persecutory but systematized and limited to the work context, consistent with a delusional disorder (ICD-10 F22). Z73.3 (stress, not elsewhere classified) and Z56.6 (other physical and mental strain related to work) were considered but do not sufficiently account for the fixed, interpretive, persecutory belief and resulting impairment.
